content:
Purpose
This document defines who may access Redwood’s sales demo environment (“demo tenant”), how access is granted, how credentials are handled, and what’s allowed during screenshare/recording. The goal is to keep demos reliable, repeatable, and safe (synthetic data only; least privilege; clean audit trail) while minimizing last-minute access issues.

This is a working draft; send edits to Markus Klein (SE demo owner) and Naomi Feldman (security/compliance advisor).


Definitions
- Demo tenant: A production-like Redwood org + projects dedicated to sales demos, seeded with synthetic usage/events so Console dashboards render realistically.
- Demo operator: An SE (or trained AE) actively running a live demo.
- Viewer: Anyone watching the demo (internal or external) without operating credentials.
- Scoped demo key: An API key with least-privilege scopes (project-limited + endpoint-limited), intended for demo scripts and sample apps.


Guiding principles
1) Synthetic-only: No customer data, no prospect data, no production logs.
2) Least privilege by default: Keys are scoped to the minimum permissions required for the standard demo scenarios.
3) No credential sharing in chat: Never paste keys into Slack, email, calendar invites, or notes visible to broad groups.
4) Auditability: All operator access must map to a named user and must be captured in audit logs.
5) Fast recovery: Keys can be rotated quickly; access issues should have a known escalation path.


Who gets access (eligible roles)
A) Default access (standing access)
- Sales Engineering (SE) team members who have completed demo certification (or are explicitly designated as demo operators by Markus Klein).
- DevEx staff supporting demo scripts (by request) when they need to validate SDK/example behavior.
- SRE/Eng Platform on-call for demo environment reliability (read-only preferred; break-glass when required).

B) Conditional access (time-bound)
- AEs running a demo solo: granted time-bound, scoped access only after completing the “AE demo operator” checklist.
- Product Marketing / Marketing: viewer-only by default; operator access only for recording production with SE support.
- Partners/SIs: no tenant access. Partners may join as viewers only on screenshare. (If a co-demo requires hands-on interaction, we use a separate partner sandbox, not the demo tenant.)

C) Not eligible
- External prospects/customers: never receive direct access to the demo tenant.
- Interns/contractors: only with explicit approval from Markus Klein + security reviewer, time-bound, and limited to viewer-only unless justified.


Access model (RBAC)
We use org-level RBAC + project-level roles.

Roles
1) Demo Operator (SE)
- Can run demo scenarios: create/read prompt sets, run evals, generate chat completions, view Console dashboards, view rollouts, manage demo routes within assigned project(s).
- Cannot: create new orgs, change billing settings, alter global security settings, export audit logs for external sharing, or modify identity provider settings.

2) Demo Viewer (Internal)
- Read-only Console access for dashboards and saved views.
- Cannot: create keys, change routes, run resets.

3) Demo Admin (Restricted)
- Very small group (owner + designated backups): can grant roles, rotate keys, trigger resets, manage seeding jobs.
- Current intended membership (draft): Markus Klein (primary), Ethan Park (backup for auth/control plane), Sean Gallagher (backup for SRE escalation).

Notes
- Anyone granted Demo Admin must have SSO + MFA enabled and be part of the audited “demo-admins” group.
- If RBAC mapping breaks (see INT-993), operator should use the escalation path below; do not workaround by sharing someone else’s session or key.


How access is requested + granted
Request paths
- Standard: Submit request in #sales-demo-ops Slack channel with:
  - Name + role (AE/SE/DevEx/SRE)
  - Reason (demo date/time + prospect)
  - Needed permissions (viewer/operator/admin)
  - Time window (start/end)
- For urgent same-day issues: page the demo on-call alias (see “Escalation”).

Approval
- Demo Operator: Markus Klein (or SE lead delegate).
- Demo Admin: Markus Klein + Sean Gallagher (or designated SRE delegate) + security reviewer sign-off.

Provisioning SLAs (targets)
- New operator access: < 1 business day.
- Urgent access fix within 2 hours during business hours; best-effort outside hours.


Credentials + API key policy
Key types
- Operator User Session: Personal SSO session used for Console access (preferred for UI demos). No shared logins.
- Scoped Demo API Keys: Used for scripted API calls (CLI/demo app). Keys must be:
  - project-scoped (no org-wide keys for demos)
  - endpoint-scoped where possible (e.g., chat only vs full API)
  - rate-limited according to demo capacity guidance

Key storage
- Keys are stored in the company password manager (1Password) in a vault named “GTM — Demo Tenant”.
- Access to the vault is limited to Demo Operators and Demo Admins.
- If a key must be temporarily provided to an operator:
  - Use 1Password item sharing (time-bound) or the internal secrets-sharing workflow.
  - Do NOT send keys via Slack DM, email, Notion/Docs, or calendar invites.

Key naming conventions
- demo/<project>/<purpose>/<owner>/<created-YYYYMMDD>
Examples:
- demo/core-api/streaming-toolcall/markus/created-20260201
- demo/obs/traffic-seed-job/mei/created-20260115

Rotation cadence
- Standard rotation: every 30 days for all scoped demo keys.
- Event-driven rotation:
  - immediately after any suspected exposure (screenshare slip, pasted into chat, repo commit)
  - after any departing employee with vault access
  - after incident where key permissions were expanded beyond baseline

Revocation
- Demo Admins can revoke keys same-day.
- When a key is revoked, the demo reset/healthcheck should be run to ensure scripts reference the new key location.

Break-glass keys
- Avoid whenever possible.
- If required for incident recovery: break-glass key must be time-bound, stored in a restricted vault, and rotated immediately after use. Document use in #sales-demo-ops with timestamp and reason.


Rules for recording, screenshots, and screensharing
Allowed to show
- Console views populated by synthetic traffic (cost/latency/error dashboards, rollouts view, traces that contain synthetic prompts).
- API responses generated live from demo prompts.
- High-level architecture diagrams for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, provided they are approved deck assets.

Not allowed to show
- Any API keys, bearer tokens, cookies, JWTs, headers, or environment variables.
- Any internal-only endpoints, internal tooling URLs, or admin panels.
- Audit logs that include internal user email addresses or internal IP/device metadata unless security has approved the specific view and the audience is internal.
- Any customer names that appear in seeded objects (seed data must remain synthetic; if you see real names, stop and report).

Operational do’s/don’ts during screenshare
- Before sharing: close password managers, terminal tabs with env vars, and any Slack DMs that might contain secrets.
- Prefer “presentation mode”: use the pre-built demo app and Console bookmarks rather than navigating raw admin pages.
- If a secret appears on screen:
  1) stop sharing
  2) rotate the impacted key (event-driven rotation)
  3) notify Demo Admin + security reviewer

Recording rules
- External recordings: Only with explicit prospect consent AND Redwood approval (AE owner + SE operator). Keep recordings in the approved shared drive folder (not personal drives).
- Internal enablement recordings: allowed, but must be treated as internal-only. Store in “GTM Enablement” drive with restricted access.
- Never publish demo tenant recordings publicly or to community channels.

Screenshots for “backup mode”
- Use pre-approved annotated screenshots (see Design task DES-611) when possible.
- If taking new screenshots:
  - ensure no secrets are visible
  - ensure the time range is set to a synthetic window
  - label as INTERNAL if it includes any admin-ish UI elements


Parallel demos (isolation expectations)
- Demos should run in isolated projects/namespaces when possible.
- Operators must not reuse the same API key for multiple parallel demos unless explicitly designated as “shared baseline demo key” with conservative quotas.
- If two demos overlap and one risks impacting the other (429s/capacity), prioritize isolating traffic by project first, then by region/model routing.


Monitoring, auditing, and compliance notes
- All key creation/rotation/revocation actions must be captured in audit logs.
- Demo environment access reviews: monthly review of:
  - who has Demo Operator access
  - who has vault access
  - which keys exist and their scopes

Security posture
- Demo tenant is not a customer environment and must not be used as a POC tenant.
- If a prospect requests hands-on access, use the POC onboarding path with a separate tenant and POC-specific keys.


Escalation & support
Primary owner: Markus Klein
Backup owners:
- Auth/RBAC issues: Ethan Park
- SLO/availability/capacity: Sean Gallagher
- Security review questions / what can be shown: Naomi Feldman

Channels
- #sales-demo-ops: day-to-day questions, access requests, known issues.
- Pager/demo-oncall (alias): live demo blocking issues (RBAC failure, 429s, dashboard empty state).

What qualifies as a “Demo Sev2”
- Live demo blocked by auth/RBAC, keys invalid, sustained 429s, or dashboards empty with no workaround inside 5 minutes.


Appendix A — Quick checklist for SEs before every demo
- Confirm you have Demo Operator role in the correct project.
- Pull keys from 1Password vault only; verify the key name matches the expected convention.
- Run demo healthcheck endpoint/report (per ENG-4862/PR-28531) and confirm:
  - model pin available
  - quotas healthy
  - synthetic traffic present (dashboards not empty)
- Confirm “do not show” items are closed (password manager, env var tabs).


Appendix B — Open questions (to resolve before final)
- Do we require demo operators to use device posture (MDM) for Console access?
- Do we allow audit log screenshots externally if we redact user identifiers in advance?
- Should AEs ever be granted operator access, or should all demos be SE-run?
- Final decision on rotation cadence (30 vs 14 days) given the frequency of live demos.

Changelog (informal)
- 2025-11-05: Initial draft created (Markus)
- 2025-11-20: Added recording/screenshot rules based on GTM feedback (Talia)
- 2026-02-12: Updated rotation + break-glass section; added links to key-scope PR and RBAC incident ticket (Ethan/Sean)
